newsitem.title: USA: L.A. utility may reassess Duke-Louis Dreyfus deal.
newsitem.headline: L.A. utility may reassess Duke-Louis Dreyfus deal.

text.p: Los Angeles Department of Water and Power (LADWP) has asked for a re-evalution of its proposed alliance with Duke-Louis Dreyfus given Duke Power Co's likely merger with PanEnergy Corp.

LADWP general manager Harry Sizemore, in a letter to L.A. city council member Ruth Galanter, said Thursday "I believe it is appropriate for the Department to review potential issues that may be raised as a result of the merger."

An ad hoc committee convened by the city council is scheduled to vote Monday on the proposed alliance with Duke-Dreyfus, a joint venture between the North Carolina utility and Louis Dreyfus Natural Gas Corp.
But Sizemore requested the proposal be returned to the LADWP for additional review before the committee takes action.
The alliance was approved in February by the LADWP board of commissioners, but must still be approved by the City Council.
Earlier this week, the U.S. Federal Energy Regulatory Commission approved the $7.7 merger of Duke with natural gas marketer and pipeline company PanEnergy.

The selection of Duke-Dreyfus as a partner for the Los Angeles municipal utility has been protested by Edison International's Southern California Edison Co, which argued that the original bidding was unfair because it did not include California utilities.
In late February, Edison sweetened its bid to partner with neighboring LADWP by adding NGC Corp to the mix and guaranteeing the municipal utility $30 million over three years.
